question:
Which of the following correctly describes water bodies in the India Desert?

1. Streams remain perennial throughout the year.

2. Most streams vanish into sandy terrain.

Which is correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Desert**, also known as the **Thar Desert**, is characterized by its arid climate and sandy terrain.
 
• The streams in the desert region do not remain perennial throughout the year due to the **extreme arid conditions** and **low rainfall**. Most streams in the Thar Desert are seasonal and dry up during summers. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• Most streams in the Indian Desert vanish into the **sandy terrain** due to the porous nature of the sand, which allows water to seep in quickly. This phenomenon is common in arid regions with sandy landscapes. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
• Examples of such streams include the **Luni River**, which flows through Rajasthan but eventually disappears into the desert sands.
 
• The presence of **endorheic basins** (closed drainage basins) in the desert region further supports the disappearance of streams into the sandy terrain. *Hence, the correct answer is Only 2.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Desert (Thar Desert):**

 
 
• The **Thar Desert** is located in **northwestern India**, covering parts of **Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana**.
 
• It is the **largest desert in India** and the **17th largest desert in the world**, with an area of approximately **200,000 square kilometers**.
 
• The desert experiences **low rainfall**, generally less than **150 mm annually**, and extreme temperatures ranging from **50°C in summers** to **0°C in winters**.
 
 
 
• **Water Characteristics in the Thar Desert:**
 
 
• The desert region has **seasonal rivers**, such as the **Luni River**, which flow only during the monsoon season.
 
• Due to the **porous sandy soil**, water from streams and rivers quickly percolates into the ground, leading to the disappearance of water bodies.
 
• The region lacks perennial water sources, and streams often end in **endorheic basins** or evaporate due to high temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Endorheic Basins:**
 
 
• **Endorheic basins** are closed drainage systems where water does not flow into external water bodies like seas or oceans.
 
• In deserts like the Thar, streams and rivers often end in such basins, where water evaporates or seeps into the ground.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Climate Characteristics:**

 
 
• The Thar Desert has an **arid climate**, with **high evaporation rates** and low humidity levels.
 
• Rainfall is sparse, and vegetation is limited to **xerophytic plants** adapted to survive in dry conditions.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Features:**
 
 
• The desert features **dunes**, salt flats, and rocky terrain. Sand dunes cover about **50%** of the desert area.
 
• The soil is largely sandy, which results in the quick absorption of water from streams and rivers.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Water Management:**
 
 
• Water management in desert regions involves creating artificial reservoirs, rainwater harvesting, and groundwater recharge systems.
 
• Projects like the **Indira Gandhi Canal** have been implemented to provide irrigation and drinking water to the desert regions.
